:JUDGMENT:
This petition emanates from the Motor Vehicle Accident dated 17.05.2023 wherein the petitioners have sought for compensation with respect to the death of Sri Koushik B.C due to the impact of the accident.

2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved SCCH 15 4 MVC No.3877/2023 in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
It is the case of the petitioners that the petitioner No.1 is the mother and the petitioner No.2 to 6 are the sisters and brother of deceased Koushik who died in the Road Traffic Accident on 17.05.2023 due to the negligence of the drivers of the respondents both tanker and lorry.

It is submitted that on 17.05.2023 at about 8.15 a.m., deceased Koushik was riding Bajaj Pulsar motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-EX-9747 slowly, carefully and cautiously by following traffic rules on the left side of the road on NH-75, Kunigal-Bangalore Road, Near Surappanahalli,
Anjinayaswamy Temple, Kudur Hobli, Magadi Taluk, Ramanagaram District, at that time, the respondent's Gas tanker Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA- 01-AA-2950 and Diesel Tanker Lorry bearing Reg No. KA-13-C- 6539 which was driven by its drivers rashly and negligently with high speed, endangering human life and dashed against the deceased's motor cycle resulting in the accident.
3. As a result of the collision, the deceased sustained fatal injuries and subsequently was taken to government hospital, Nelamangala.
Pertinently, the injury suffered by the deceased SCCH 15 5 MVC No.3877/2023 proved to be fatal resulting in his death.

4. Consequently, on 17.05.2023 a FIR No.160/2023 was registered with the Kudur Police station under Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC and charge sheet was filed under Sec.279, 304(A) of IPC and r/w Sec.181 of IMV Act against the driver of Respondent No.5 vehicle and the deceased.
5. The Petitioners submit that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the drivers of both Gas tanker lorry and Diesel tanker lorry.

It is submitted that the deceased was hale and healthy and aged about 19 years and working as coolie and also agriculturist and was earning Rs.25,000/- p.m. at the time of accident and he was the sole bread earner and had good future prospects.
Due to untimely death of the deceased the Petitioners have lost love, affection and support which has caused mental agony to the petitioners.
Hence, the petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- with costs and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.

REASONS 12. Issue No.1: Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.

It is contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners,
that the rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle gas tanker lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AA-2950 and Diesel tanker lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-13-C-6539 drivers caused the accident.
In this regard the the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has cross-examined PW.1, PW.1 in her cross-examination has deposed that she has not witnessed the accident.
It is admitted that the deceased did not have valid driving license and hence the charge sheet has been filed against the deceased which has not been challenged by the petitioners.
It is admitted that the motorcycle of the deceased is insured with the Bajaj Allianz Insurance company.
It is admitted that the accident took place at middle of the road.
It is denied that the deceased without holding driving license and without helmet, went in between the lorries to his left and right side and lost control and fell on road, resulting in the accident.

On the other hand, the PW.1 has submitted that the lorry dashed on Shashikala vs Srirangaraj.M on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43025517/

On the other hand, in the cross-examination by respondent No.4, PW.1 has deposed the charge sheet has been filed against the deceased and tanker lorry driver and no charge sheet has been filed against the diesel tanker lorry.

14. The respondent No.2 Legal Manager has been examined SCCH 15 11 MVC No.3877/2023 as RW.1 and in her cross-examination she has deposed that two tanker lorries are involved in the accident however, there is no fault on the part of the driver of lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AA- 2950.
It is denied that the accident took place due to the fault of both the tanker lorry drivers.
It is admitted that the charge sheet is filed against the respondent No.1 vehicle and against the deceased.

15. In the light of the said admissions in the cross- examination of PW.1 and RW.1 on perusal of the charge sheet documents it discloses that the charge sheet has been filed by the police after investigation against the deceased himself and driver of gas lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AA-2950.

It is submitted in the charge sheet that deceased Koushik did not have valid driving license and he rode the motorcycle in rash and negligent manner and without any indication turned the bike to the right side and fell on the road and at that time the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01- AA-2950 lost control and went over the deceased resulting in the accident.

As far as diesel lorry is concerned no rash or negligence is made out since due to the impact the gas lorry subsequently collided with diesel lorry and hence no charge sheet is filed against SCCH 15 12 MVC No.3877/2023 diesel lorry.
16.

On perusal of the spot sketch it discloses that the accident has taken place on the middle of the road and the damages to the vehicle discloses that the motorcycle ridden by the deceased is completely damaged and there are damages on the diesel lorry vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-C-6539 due to collusion by gas lorry itself.
PW.1 is not an eye witness to the accident.

Hence, taking into consideration the evidence and the charge sheet documents there is no doubt that the accident occurred due to the irresponsible and negligence riding of the deceased himself without having any valid driving license.
In addition there is negligence on the part of driver of gas lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AA-2950.

Hence, this Court is of the opinion that the accident could have been avoided if the deceased could have ridden his motorcycle with due care while riding on the middle of the road and between heavy goods vehicles.
The evidence as per the charge sheet and PW.1 categorically discloses that accident has taken place on the middle of the road.
Hence, if the deceased would have taken proper care at the time of riding in the middle of the road the unfortunate SCCH 15 13 MVC No.3877/2023 accident could have been avoided.
The rash and negligent driving does not in every case necessarily mean the excessive speed.
Not taking due care while driving the vehicle and in particular overtaking, either stationary or moving vehicle also would amount to rash and negligent driving as held in catena of decisions.
Hence, I am of the considered view that the deceased is guilty of contributory negligence to the accident to the extent of 20%.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 "Partly in the Affirmative ".

19. Issue No.3: Computation of compensation under the various heads is assessed as follows:
 SCCH 15 15 MVC No.3877/2023  1. Loss of dependency Age factor:

In order to assess the compensation under the head of loss of dependency the age,
avocation and income of the deceased needs to be ascertained.
In the present case, the age of the deceased is shown as 19 years.
Ex.P-17 is the Aadhaar card which shows that the date of birth of the deceased is 08.04.2004.
The alleged accident has taken place on 17.05.2023.
Hence, the age of the deceased at the time of accident is 19 years, 1 month, 9 days.
Hence, by considering Ex.P17, the age of the deceased is taken as 20 years.
20. Income and avocation:
It is stated in the evidence that deceased was working as a Coolie and also an agriculturist and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
The Petitioners have not produced any documentary evidence or adduced the evidence of the employer or any salary payment receipts to prove the actual income of the deceased.
Hence in the absence of evidence to prove the actual income of the deceased the notional income will have to be taken into consideration.
Looking into the age of the deceased and the avocation it is just and proper to fix the notional income of SCCH 15 16 MVC No.3877/2023 the deceased as Rs.16,000/- per month.
Therefore, the Annual Income of the deceased would be 16,000X 12= 1,92,000/-.

Hence for the purpose of computation of Claim, the annual income of the deceased is taken as Rs.1,92,000/-.
21.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121 has established the golden principles in considering compensation in cases of death.

The criteria which are to be taken into consideration for assessing compensation in the case of death are: (i) the age of the deceased at the time of his death; (ii) the number of dependents left behind by the deceased; and (iii) the income of the deceased at the time of his death.
If these determinants are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in these decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will be SCCH 15 17 MVC No.3877/2023 easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
"Step 1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand) The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance, which is considered to be the contribution to the dependant family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step 2 (Ascertaining the multiplier) Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a Table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said Table with reference to the age of the deceased."

Moving forward with the issue of future prospects, the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680, held that Future prospects are to be awarded on the basis of:
(i) The nature of the deceased's employment; and (ii) The age of the deceased.

Hence while calculating the deductions towards the personal expenses, the number of dependents at the time of the death of the deceased is to be considered.

As per the dicta of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma (supra), since the deceased was a bachelor, the deductions towards the personal expenses would be 1/2.

In this Petition, the deceased was aged 20 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 40% of the income has to be added.
So, 40% of Rs.16,000/- comes to Rs.6,400/-.

Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.22,400/- p.m. (Rs.16,000/- + Rs.6,400/- =
Rs.22,400/-).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 18.

after a period of 3 years.

28. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the drivers of the offending Gas Tanker Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AA-2950.

As per the detailed discussion made in Issue No.1, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the driver of the offending vehicle attributes 80% of contributory negligence and the rider / deceased of the Bajaj Pulsar motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-EX-9747 attributes 20%

In this case, the Respondent SCCH 15 23 MVC No.3877/2023 No.1 is the Owner and Respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the offending Gas lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AA-2950.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.

Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy 80%
of the the award amount out of the total award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay 80% of the compensation amount to the Petitioners.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 and 3 "Partly in the Affirmative".

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On perusal of the spot sketch it discloses that the accident has taken place on the middle of the road and the damages to the vehicle discloses that the motorcycle ridden by the deceased is completely damaged and there are damages on the diesel lorry vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-C-6539 due to collusion by gas lorry itself.
PW.1 is not an eye witness to the accident.
Hence, taking into consideration the evidence and the charge sheet documents there is no doubt that the accident occurred due to the irresponsible and negligence riding of the deceased himself without having any valid driving license.
In addition there is negligence on the part of driver of gas lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AA-2950.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that the accident could have been avoided if the deceased could have ridden his motorcycle with due care while riding on the middle of the road and between heavy goods vehicles.
The evidence as per the charge sheet and PW.1 categorically discloses that accident has taken place on the middle of the road.
Hence, if the deceased would have taken proper care at the time of riding in the middle of the road the unfortunate SCCH 15 13 MVC No.3877/2023 accident could have been avoided.
The rash and negligent driving does not in every case necessarily mean the excessive speed.
Not taking due care while driving the vehicle and in particular overtaking, either stationary or moving vehicle also would amount to rash and negligent driving as held in catena of decisions.
Though the Petitioner No.1 is the mother and Petitioner No. 2 to 5 are the majors and petitioner No.2 is married sister and Petitioner No.6 is the Minor sister of the deceased, being the legal representatives of deceased Koushik have a right to apply for compensation.
As the Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Koushik and also they have proved that the death of the Koushik has been caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, they are entitled for the compensation.
Hence in the absence of evidence to prove the actual income of the deceased the notional income will have to be taken into consideration.
Looking into the age of the deceased and the avocation it is just and proper to fix the notional income of SCCH 15 16 MVC No.3877/2023 the deceased as Rs.16,000/- per month.
Therefore, the Annual Income of the deceased would be 16,000X 12= 1,92,000/-.
Hence for the purpose of computation of Claim, the annual income of the deceased is taken as Rs.1,92,000/-.
